subject: GlacierPay — sudden throughput & latency spike after model rollforward
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@glacierpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Moreno <elena@glacierpay.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production anomaly — latency & error spike after model update

Jordan / Laura —

We just observed a sharp jump in p95 latency and a spike in 5xx error rates starting at 14:48 UTC after your rollout. Key customer-facing metrics: p95 from ~320ms to ~1.1s, p99 to ~2.8s, and a transient 5xx error rate peaking at 6.4% for the payments-parsing route. Throughput dropped by ~25% on the hot path (tokenization-heavy flows).

Attached is a screenshot from our dashboard and a sample error trace (glacierpay_error_snapshot.png). This impact is customer-visible — several transactions timed out and failed reconciliation jobs queued up. Can you confirm whether the recent model rollforward or a quant profile change was applied to our tenant around 14:40 UTC?

We need an immediate remediation plan and an ETA for rollback if necessary. Happy to join an urgent call.

—Sanjay
Head of Integrations, GlacierPay
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@glacierpay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production anomaly — latency & error spike after model update

Sanjay — thank you for the heads up and the artifacts. We saw the same signal on our side. Short answers first: yes, there was a scheduled rollforward at 14:37 UTC that flipped GlacierPay to model v4.3-int8 (quantized profile) as part of the staged rollout.

Immediate plan:
- Stand up a 15-min incident huddle (joining link: https://meet.redwood.ai/incident/INF-4821) — Vivek and Rishi are on-call.
- We can either route traffic back to v4.2 (previous production variant) or apply an emergency canary to reduce exposure.
- Would you prefer an automatic rollback to the prior variant (fastest) or to continue on v4.3 while we throttle/route to canary and gather traces (safer for investigating root cause)?

I’ll keep this thread live and send a short exec note once we decide. Laura, can you coordinate customer comms and credits if we roll back? Rishi / Vivek — please share a short diagnostic ASAP.

—Jordan
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production anomaly — latency & error spike after model update

On Mon, Jul 19, 2027 at 3:25 PM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I’ll keep this thread live and send a short exec note once we decide.

Quick diagnostic from infra: initial traces show a pattern consistent with an attention-kernel slowdown under int8 at longer sequence lengths. Two likely contributing factors:
- The v4.3-int8 variant introduced a micro-optimization that changed KV cache flush timing when requests include long prompt prefixes; this increases per-request decode time for hot paths.
- We’re also seeing a tokenization mismatch in ~0.7% of requests that triggers fallback logic and additional endpoint retries — that amplifies latency and 5xx counts under load.

We captured a perf profile (perf_profile_int8_stub.json) and a small set of failing request IDs. Short remediations:
1) Emergency rollback to v4.2 (fastest, will restore prior perf).
2) If customer prefers no rollback, we can throttle v4.3 traffic and apply a targeted fix to KV cache flush behavior (estimate ~8–12 hours to test + deploy).

I recommend rollback as stop-gap and then a controlled re-roll with an adjusted quant profile.

—Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production anomaly — latency & error spike after model update

On Mon, Jul 19, 2027 at 3:33 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I recommend rollback as stop-gap and then a controlled re-roll with an adjusted quant profile.

Agree with rollback. Operational plan (if GlacierPay approves):
- 15:55 UTC: flip GlacierPay route back to v4.2 (previous stable variant) via routing policy (no infra deploy).
- 15:55–16:05 UTC: monitor p50/p95/p99 and 5xx; if metrics return within baseline, keep v4.2 while we investigate.
- Post-mortem: pulse check and detailed RCA within 48 hours; deliverable: timeline + remediation + regression test case.

Risks & notes:
- Rolling back will increase cost while we run canaries (temporary, expected).
- If rollback is blocked, we can apply a conservative throttling policy to reduce token-heavy requests and enable an emergency tokenization patch (longer ETA).

I’ll prepare the rollback runbook and the step to pin the model variant. ETA for runbook and a Slack incident channel: 10 minutes.

—Vivek
VP, Serving Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@glacierpay.com>, Elena Moreno <elena@glacierpay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production anomaly — latency & error spike after model update

Sanjay / Elena —

Thanks for the quick report and patience. Per Rishi/Vivek’s recommendation we propose an emergency rollback to v4.2 starting at 15:55 UTC (this is the fastest way to restore normal latency & error rates). Specifics:
- Action: Route GlacierPay traffic back to model v4.2 (no code deploy).
- Window: 15:55–16:05 UTC monitor; we will keep you updated every 5 minutes during the window.
- Post-action: Full RCA and regression test; we’ll share the rollback runbook and a remediation timeline.

As a gesture for the impact, Redwood will apply a goodwill credit for July usage tied to the incident (Laura — please manage). We will not proceed without your explicit consent to roll back.

Attached: rollback-plan.pdf (short runbook + monitoring checklist). Please reply with APPROVE to proceed. If you prefer to avoid rollback, say so and we’ll apply throttling/canary instead.

—Jordan
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@glacierpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Moreno <elena@glacierpay.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@glacierpay.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production anomaly — latency & error spike after model update

Jordan —

APPROVE to roll back to v4.2. Please proceed immediately and keep us posted. We appreciate the offer of a credit; procurement will follow up with Laura on formal SLA remediation. Also, we request a post-mortem with the regression test case and a timeline for when v4.3 can be reintroduced (we can tolerate a brief delay as long as regressions are prevented).

I’m on the incident call now.

—Sanjay
Head of Integrations, GlacierPay
